title: introduce lightweight auth-proxy + typed sink facade to harmonize retries across py/ts/go
author: Linnea Ortiz
description:
Motivation: teams building on multiple SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) were duplicating credential refresh and retry wiring for streaming use-cases. This PR introduces a tiny auth-proxy shim and a language-agnostic "typed sink" facade to provide a single retry/telemetry surface while preserving idiomatic consumer ergonomics per SDK. The change improves parity across SDKs (error mapping, backoff presets) and reduces duplicated token-refresh logic in downstream customers.

Summary of changes (single-line sections separated by newlines for readability):
- Introduce auth_proxy interface (minimal surface): GetToken(), OnFailure(hint) and Probe(). Implement lightweight adapters for Py/TS/Go so existing SDKs can call a common orchestration in the control plane.
- Add TypedSink facade: StreamSink<T> / AsyncStreamSink in each SDK that exposes a small set of operations (open, write, drain, close) with built-in retry presets and cancel-aware drains.
- Add retry profile mapping: "interactive", "throughput", "best_effort" presets used by the sink. The profiles are tunable via SDK config and emitted as telemetry tags.
- Parity fixes: align SDK error codes for EOF/Cancel/RateLimit and make session-ttl jitter consistent across languages.
- Telemetry: add retry_reason and sink_profile tags to span/metric emissions for downstream billing and SLO analysis.
- Version bumps: python -> 2.5.0, typescript -> 1.28.0, go -> 1.8.0 (minor SDK bumps for compatibility).
- Docs: add example snippets for idiomatic usage in py/ts/go quickstarts, and a short migration note for teams using the older PullStream helpers.

Why this is different from previous "cred/stream" PRs: instead of importing large credential orchestration into each SDK, this adds a tiny, composable shim that lets the control plane (or a thin local adapter) own heavy lifecycle work while the SDK exposes a consistent sink API. The focus is on ergonomics for streaming producers/consumers rather than introducing new session protocols.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(auth): add auth_proxy interface and basic adapters (py/ts/go)
- feat(stream): add typed sink facade and profile mapping in SDK runtimes
- perf(test): add cross-sdk unit tests for retry mapping and cancel semantics
- docs: quickstart examples and migration guide
- ci: bump SDK versions and pin compatibility matrix

Files/touched (high-level):
- sdk/python/redwood/stream_sink.py (new) + tests/sdk_python/test_stream_sink.py
- sdk/typescript/src/sink/typedSink.ts (new) + examples/ts/stream-sink.md
- sdk/go/sink/typed_sink.go (new) + sink/sink_test.go
- internal/auth/proxy.go (new adapter) and internal/auth/proxy_py_binding.py
- docs/streaming/migration/typed-sink.md
- ci/versions.yaml (version bumps)

Checklist: 
- [x] Add auth-proxy interface and adapters
- [x] Implement typed sink in each SDK with basic unit tests
- [x] CI green on retries/streaming matrix (flaky test rerun once)
- [x] Docs and migration notes included
- [x] Version bumps coordinated with release automation

CI notes: initial CI run showed a flaky interop test (sdk/typescript/test/stream_integration) failing with a 1/120 timeout; test was flakey due to local test harness timing and was re-run; subsequent pipeline passed. All checks green on the final run.

Review highlights / conversation in PR thread: note that the full thread is summarized here rather than including the entire timeline.
- Priya: asked to ensure that OnFailure only returns advisory hints and not full token refreshs; requested a small API doc for the proxy contract.
- Author (Linnea): responded with API doc and a small unit-test proving OnFailure is advisory; left an implementation note describing how control plane may implement heavier logic.
- Ethan: requested clearer backoff semantics for the "interactive" profile (added explicit 50ms-500ms tier in mapping table and unit tests).
- Jonas: requested additional telemetry tag for "sink_role" (producer/consumer) — added.
- Final: approved after minor test and doc updates.

Migration guidance (short):
- For teams using legacy PullStream helpers, switch to StreamSink.open(), write(), drain(), close(). The adapter layer will still accept old PullStream objects for a deprecation window.
- If you previously implemented refresh-on-401 in client code, prefer providing an auth_proxy adapter to avoid multiple competing refreshers.

Release notes:
- Adds a compact auth-proxy shim and typed sink facade for Py/TS/Go SDKs; improves streaming ergonomics and cross-language parity.
- SDK minor version bumps: py 2.5.0, ts 1.28.0, go 1.8.0.
- No breaking API changes; migration adapters included for legacy PullStream helpers.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: customers implementing custom refresh loops may observe duplicate refresh attempts. Mitigation: adapter includes a no-op registration path plus an opt-in dedupe helper; documentation highlights the recommended pattern.
- Risk: telemetry volume increase from retry tags. Mitigation: tags are optional behind a config flag and default sampling is unchanged.

Next steps / follow-ups (future PRs):
- Add canary rollout of the typed sink defaults for Hosted API routes.
- Surface sink_profile recommendations in Redwood Optimize as workload suggestions.

Overall outcome: merged to main via squash. This PR reduces duplicated credentials logic in customer code and gives a consistent streaming producer surface across the three SDKs while keeping each language ergonomic and idiomatic.
